records.title: Engineering human biology In vitro: a comparative assessment of biodesign, manufacturing and validation strategies for next-generation non-animal models and new approach methodologies.
records.abstract: Animal models have long underpinned pre-clinical biomedical research, but ethical concerns, cost, species differences and frequent discordance between animal and clinical outcomes have driven the search for human-relevant alternatives. Non-animal models, which overlap with but are not synonymous with New Approach Methodologies (NAMs; a regulatory term whose definition is still evolving), now include 3D spheroids and organoids, organ-on-chip systems, 3D bioprinted tissues, the in ovo chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model and AI-enabled in silico tools. Rather than describing each technology in isolation, this review compares them on cost, throughput, biological complexity, reproducibility, regulatory qualification status, manufacturing maturity and potential for adoption, and benchmarks them against animal models where concordance data exist. It treats engineering as a central topic, examining biomaterial reproducibility, automation, GMP-adjacent production and quality control as the factors that currently limit clinical and industrial translation. Only a few platforms tested against well-defined endpoints, such as the Liver-Chip for drug-induced liver injury and reconstructed human epidermis for skin irritation, have shown quantitative parity with, or superiority to, animal benchmarks; most organoid, spheroid and multi-organ systems remain limited by variability, incomplete vascularisation and a lack of prospective, blinded validation. Regulators and standards bodies in the European Union, the USA, the UK, China, India and elsewhere are increasingly enabling NAMs, yet limited validation, lack of standards and institutional inertia persist. We outline mitigation strategies, including defined matrices, automation, staged multi-laboratory validation and tiered testing in which NAMs complement animal studies, and discuss opportunities for future adoption.

records.title: Human blood-brain barrier models for intracerebral hemorrhage: From conventional in vitro systems to advanced microphysiological platforms.
records.abstract: Intracerebral bleeding (ICH), the deadliest type of bleeding stroke, has always been a significant source of death and neurological disability all around the world. Despite extensive laboratory research, translating trial therapies into real-world practice has been limited because current animal models are often not clinically relevant. At the same time, it is widely recognized that there is a strong need for newly developed blood-brain barrier models. Recent breakthroughs in tissue engineering, stem cell theory, materials science, and microfabrication have enabled the creation of new blood-brain barrier models. These include moist and dry Transwell-based co-culture models, three-dimensional hydrogel-supported models, human pluripotent stem cell-based models, multicellular spheroids and organoids, and microfluidic blood-brain barrier devices and organoids that can operate under perfusion conditions. Each new model offers clear advantages for blood-brain barrier research, but also has serious disadvantages. This review critically analyses current in vitro human BBB models in the context of ICH pathophysiology and explains their formulations, translational applications, advantages, and disadvantages. It also describes new tools that use biomaterials, vascularisation, and dynamic perfusion to improve model fidelity. Hence, new-generation human BBB model platforms may pave the way for replacing animal models in explaining disease mechanisms, developing therapies, and improving precision medicine for ICH.

records.title: Perineural invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma: clinical evidence and mechanistic hypotheses.
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a major cause of cancer mortality worldwide. Emerging evidence in cancer neuroscience suggests that tumor-nerve crosstalk can modulate tumor growth, immune remodeling, dissemination, and therapy resistance. Perineural invasion (PNI) is a hallmark of aggressive tumors and correlates with recurrence, metastasis, disease-specific death, and neuropathic pain, yet its prevalence and prognostic relevance in primary HCC remain inconsistently defined. Given the limited and heterogeneous clinical data, we synthesize available observations and propose mechanistic hypotheses for neural-tumor interactions in the hepatic niche. Potential drivers are organized into five domains-neurotrophic factors, axon guidance molecules, neurotransmitter signaling, cell adhesion molecules, and the tumor microenvironment-highlighting neuro-immune-stromal circuits that may create permissive perineural niches. We also outline experimental platforms to test these hypotheses, including co-culture systems, organoids, and microfluidic nerve-on-chip models. Targeting neural-tumor interactions may offer translational opportunities in HCC, but causality and actionable targets cannot be established without improved clinical and experimental rigor. Standardized pathological assessment and dedicated HCC-focused PNI models are needed to validate mechanisms, harmonize reporting, and enable reproducible, clinically meaningful advances.

records.title: Rnf43 loss or forced CDX2 with active Kras/GNAS induces intestinal-type intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm of the pancreas via targetable Wnt/PI3K.
records.abstract: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN) of the intestinal type is characterized by dilated pancreatic ducts filled with thick mucin and lined by high-grade neoplastic papillae. These neoplastic cells express CDX2 and frequently harbor KRAS, GNAS, and RNF43 mutations. While existing GNAS/KRAS mouse models recapitulate gastric-type IPMN, no intestinal-type IPMN model has been reported. We aimed to develop an intestinal-type IPMN mouse model and investigate its oncogenic signaling. We crossed Pdx1Cre/+;LSL-KrasG12D;Tg(CAG-LSL-GNASR201H) (PKG) mice with Rnf43 knockout or Rosa26-CAG-LSL-hCDX2 mice to generate models with active Kras and GNAS combined with heterozygous (PKGR +/- ) or homozygous (PKGR-/-) Rnf43 deficiency, or forced pancreatic hCDX2 expression (PKGC). Phenotypes were histopathologically examined. Isolated tumor cells were evaluated in organoid cultures, and PI3K and Wnt inhibitors were tested in vitro and in vivo. Compared with PKG mice, PKGR +/- and PKGR-/- mice showed significantly poorer survival. PKGC mice tended to exhibit a shorter lifespan. All these models developed significantly larger pancreatic tumors than PKG mice. Tumors exhibited multiple dilated ducts, high-grade dysplastic papillary epithelial proliferation, acid mucin production and MUC2 expression, consistent with intestinal-type IPMN phenotypes. In vitro, Wnt and PI3K/AKT signaling increased, while PKA signaling decreased; Wnt or AKT inhibition suppressed cell proliferation. In vivo treatment with a Wnt inhibitor prolonged survival and attenuated tumorigenesis. Activated Wnt and PI3K signaling, driven by Rnf43 deficiency or CDX2 expression alongside active Kras and GNAS, promotes phenotypic changes associated with intestinal-type IPMN. Wnt inhibition suppresses tumor cell proliferation, highlighting a potential molecularly targeted strategy for high-grade IPMN.

records.title: Contractile function maintains cardiomyocyte differentiation and inhibits cell cycle activity.
records.abstract: The human heart loses regenerative capacity shortly after birth, a time at which cardiomyocytes undergo vast transcriptional changes that enhance their contractility and efficiency. This is suggested to underlie the restricted proliferative potential of cardiomyocytes. Whether the strong cardiovascular function required for the mammalian heart directly contributes to the cell cycle blockade remains to be explored. Here, we use human cardiac organoids combined with direct targeting of contraction using mavacamten and aficamten to enable exquisite control of active contraction over brief time windows. We show that transient inhibition of contraction reactivates the cell cycle. Multi-omics analyses demonstrated that the cell cycle response is mediated through a de-differentiation-like process involving rapid sarcomere remodeling and metabolic adaptations, including AKT1-mediated and PDK-mediated cell cycle activation. The de-differentiation response was swiftly reversed upon removal of the myosin inhibitors. Together these findings reveal that active contraction maintains cardiac maturity, including cell cycle arrest in cardiomyocytes.

records.title: Liver-on-chip: engineering translational models for liver diseases.
records.abstract: Chronic liver diseases and cancers remain a major global health challenge. Despite significant advances, effective treatment options remain limited, particularly for advanced diseases. The limited clinical translatability of the conventional preclinical models has hampered therapeutic development. Two-dimensional cultures poorly reproduce the complex hepatic architecture, metabolic zonation, and multicellular crosstalk, while animal models often fail to reflect human-specific physio pathological and pharmacological responses. Three-dimensional (3D) spheroids and organoids have improved physiological relevance by restoring cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions, enabling the modeling of steatosis, fibrosis, viral hepatitis, and primary liver cancers. However, their static nature limits long-term stability and functional maturation. In this context, liver-on-a-chip (LoC) technologies have emerged as promising platforms that combine 3D models with microfluidics and extracellular matrix components to better recapitulate human liver physiology and pathology ex vivo. By introducing controlled perfusion, mechanical stimuli and biochemical gradients, LoC systems enhance tissue organization and functional performance. These platforms are also increasingly investigated for drug-induced liver injury (DILI), where human-relevant models may improve the detection and mechanistic characterization of hepatotoxicity. Importantly, by providing human-relevant physiology ex vivo, these advanced 3D models and LoC platforms have the potential to reduce reliance on animal experiments. However, the development of a robust and physiologically relevant LoC model requires careful consideration of multiple interdependent parameters. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the key components that define LoC systems, including microfluidic design, cellular sources, and extracellular matrix selection. Moreover, we highlight opportunities of LoC models for modeling clinical pathology, DILI assessment and therapeutic discovery.

records.title: A Testable Framework for Mechanics-Conditioned Perturbation Models in Drug Discovery.
records.abstract: Perturbation-predictive cell models are advancing quickly, yet they remain predominantly molecular, even though the mechanical state of cells and tissues-stiffness, viscoelasticity, geometry, and force generation-can alter therapeutic response. This review converts that observation into a testable program. It separates four claims that are routinely conflated and gives each its own baseline, estimand, design, and named refutation condition: whether auxiliary mechanical measurements improve prediction of treatment response beyond a complete non-mechanical baseline (H1); whether mechanics computed from images help as a representation rather than as added information (H2); whether experimentally controlled mechanical context modifies treatment effects, including once local drug exposure is held comparable (H3 and H3a); and whether mechanics-aware predictions improve preclinical prioritization decisions under a fixed budget (H4). Current evidence is graded against an explicit, reproducible rubric, and the two links the framework actually requires, mechanical conditioning of perturbation response and prospectively validated mechanics-aware decisions, are unpopulated. A worked pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma program specifies donors, materials, gemcitabine exposure measurement, endpoints, simulation-based power, staged costs, and a blinded decision test, with a reduced-scope minimum implementation for groups that cannot execute the full design. The practical contribution for a bioengineering readership is a transferable specification checklist, covering measurement provenance, units of assignment and inference, leakage control, effect margins, and decision rules, to be completed before resources are committed. We conclude that mechanics should enter perturbation models as a hypothesis carrying a refutation condition, not as a default enrichment. Explicit limitations bound the work: the synthesis is targeted rather than systematic, the evidence grades were assigned by a single assessor, and the framework has not itself been executed.

records.title: Digital Twins in Oncology: Current Evidence, Multiscale Modeling Approaches, and Challenges in Clinical Translation-A Narrative Review.
records.abstract: Digital Twin (DT), a dynamic simulation technology derived from the engineering field, has been deeply integrated into the field of tumor precision medicine, empowered by both multi-omics technologies and artificial intelligence. It offers a novel approach to overcoming the limitations of traditional paradigms in tumor research, diagnosis, and treatment. This article reviews the full-scale application system of tumor DT, spanning from the molecular to the individual level, and constructs a progressive simulation architecture of "virtual cell-virtual knockout/virtual overexpression-virtual organoid-virtual patient". The virtual cell enables the in silico representation of tumor cells and the tumor microenvironment, serving as the fundamental unit for dissecting molecular mechanisms. Virtual knockout/overexpression provides non-invasive, high-throughput methods for target prioritization, significantly shortening research and development cycles. The virtual organoid achieves computational reconstruction of the three-dimensional (3D) tumor microenvironment, bridging the gap between single-cell and individual-scale simulations. The virtual patient, in turn, supports personalized therapeutic decision-making and virtual clinical trials. By synthesizing the latest research findings in the field, this article delineates the technical pathways, primary modeling tools, and representative empirical cases for each application tier. It further provides an in-depth analysis of core challenges, including multi-source data heterogeneity, insufficient model accuracy and interpretability, and obstacles to clinical translation. Corresponding solutions, such as data standardization, cross-scale technology integration, and interdisciplinary collaboration between medicine and engineering, are proposed. The aim is to provide a comprehensive reference for leveraging DT to advance tumor research and facilitate its translation into clinical practice.

records.title: SparseKG-Flow: A Virtual Cell Generative Architecture Unifying Structural Causal Models and Knowledge Graph Priors for Single-Cell Drug Perturbation Prediction.
records.abstract: Predicting single-cell responses to new drugs is essential for mechanism-aware virtual cell modeling, yet existing models often fail on unseen drugs or cell types by relying on memorized correlations rather than transferable mechanisms. SparseKG-Flow addresses this out-of-distribution (OOD) challenge as a generative architecture integrating three inductive biases: a sparse drug-effect encoder with Gumbel-Softmax gating, a heterogeneous graph adapter for drug-target-pathway knowledge, and a mechanism-guided residual flow decoder. On Tahoe-100M, it achieves Pearson r of 0.942 and 0.920 under Test-NewDrug and Test-NewCell settings, respectively, outperforming the next-best baseline by 16.6% and 14.8%. It also reduces Δ expression error by 89.0% and 91.7%, respectively, and more than doubles held-out-drug top-gene recovery (Overlap@50 = 0.210). Frozen-model evaluation on high-grade serous ovarian cancer patient data provides preliminary evidence of transfer beyond the Tahoe-100M panel. Ablations confirm all components aid OOD generalization, with the molecular knowledge adapter contributing the most. SparseKG-Flow further reorganizes pharmacological priors into interpretable, task-trained representations and highlights Abemaciclib, Capmatinib, and Gemcitabine in A549 analysis. It thus serves as both an accurate perturbation predictor and a mechanism-grounded virtual cell platform for therapeutic prioritization.

records.title: MitoLODE: a virtual mitochondrion framework with knowledge graph priors for trajectory modeling and mechanistic perturbation analysis.
records.abstract: Mitochondria play a central role in the pathogenesis of major diseases. Tracking how they evolve under disease conditions is valuable for understanding pathological mechanisms and identifying intervention windows. Existing single-cell trajectory inference methods rely on pseudotime rather than a real temporal axis, and rarely model disease and control as independent trajectories. Virtual cell methods target one-shot drug perturbation responses and do not handle the continuous temporal evolution of disease phenotypes. To address these gaps, we propose a virtual mitochondrion research paradigm. We first curate and construct MitoKG, a mitochondria-specific heterogeneous knowledge graph integrated from five authoritative databases. MitoKG contains 2549 nodes of four types and 23 019 edges of five relation types. Building on these priors, we develop MitoLODE, a conditioned dual-trajectory neural ordinary differential equation framework. MitoLODE embeds graph priors and temporal features throughout encoding, continuous-time dynamics, and decoding, modeling disease and control evolution as two coupled paths. Benchmarked against eight baselines across four datasets covering Parkinson's disease, cardiac, and pancreatic differentiation, MitoLODE leads in most settings and remains robust under low-data regimes and extrapolation to unseen time points. Two synthetic datasets with known ground truth validate its trajectory recovery under controlled conditions. Building on the trained model, we design a gradient-guided perturbation procedure that identifies potential intervention targets aligned with known Parkinson's pathology. We develop MGMI, a large language model-based reasoning module that grounds model outputs in MitoKG nodes and turns them into confidence-graded mechanistic hypotheses, which nonetheless require experimental validation.

records.title: Virtual Knockout in the Era of Generative AI: From Intracellular Networks to Spatial and Cross-Modal Functional Simulations.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation data have enabled computational models that predict intervention-associated cellular responses. This narrative review organizes explicit gene-regulatory-network simulations, latent and compositional response models, graph, optimal-transport, and dynamical approaches, foundation-model representations, and emerging spatial or cross-modal settings through a virtual-knockout lens. We distinguish representation-level ablation from causal genetic intervention and separate held-out regimes for genes, cell types or contexts, perturbation combinations, chemical structures, and doses. We compare representative methods, experimental resources, metrics, and benchmark frameworks and operationally define a prospective holographic virtual cell by its modalities, regulatory and physical constraints, intervention-conditioned outputs with calibrated uncertainty, and prospective validation requirements. The holographic virtual cell and Design-Build-Test-Learn roadmap are presented as future-facing criteria rather than as an achieved clinical capability.

records.title: Engineering of Microbial Cell Factories for Flavonoid Production: from Flavanone Platforms to Tailored Derivatives.
records.abstract: Flavonoids are valuable plant polyphenols used in foods, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals. However, their production is limited by the low abundance of many flavonoids in plants and the structural complexity that complicates chemical synthesis. Microbial cell factories provide a sustainable alternative, yet engineering requirements increase sharply from platform flavanones to oxidized and multiply tailored derivatives. This Review organizes recent advances according to product complexity, covering flavanones, oxidized flavones and flavonols, and methylated, glycosylated, and prenylated flavonoids. We examine the major constraints at each product level, including aromatic precursor and malonyl-CoA supply, enzyme activity and selectivity, redox and oxygen demands, and the regeneration of activated methyl, sugar, and prenyl donors. We further highlight the need to coordinate scaffold formation, oxidation, tailoring reactions, donor regeneration, and host metabolism rather than optimizing individual pathway steps independently. Finally, emerging artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted strategies for enzyme engineering, demand-responsive pathway regulation, automated design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycles, and virtual-cell modeling are discussed. This product-complexity-oriented framework provides design principles for developing efficient, modular, and programmable microbial platforms for flavonoid biomanufacturing.

records.title: Deep generative protein design needs a lab partner.
records.abstract: Deep generative models have revolutionized protein design and engineering, but generating proteins with desirable application-relevant phenotypic properties remains a challenge. Recent work is beginning to move beyond workflows in which experiments provide post hoc validation of computational designs toward the integrated use of experimental data to shape what generative models learn, propose, and optimize. In this review, we survey recent approaches organized under three prevailing paradigms through which experimental information enters the design process: post-training alignment, inference-time steering, and closed-loop design. We compare the methodological approaches and their respective advantages, limitations, and data requirements and consider applications spanning binding, fluorescence, stability, expression, activity, and specificity. We propose that realizing the full potential of deep generative protein design requires a unified framework in which generative models, quantitative assays, and automated experimental platforms are developed together and experimental measurements actively guide and refine the design process.

records.title: MolSnap: Snap-fast molecular generation with latent variational mean flow.
records.abstract: Molecular generation conditioned on textual descriptions is a fundamental task in computational chemistry and drug discovery. Existing methods often struggle to simultaneously ensure high-quality, diverse generation and fast inference. In this work, we propose a novel framework that addresses these challenges through two key innovations. First, we introduce a Causality-Aware Transformer (CAT) that jointly encodes molecular graph tokens and text instructions while imposing a directional sequential inductive bias during generation. Second, we develop a Variational Mean Flow (VMF) framework that generalizes existing flow-based methods by modeling a mixture of predicted velocities, enhancing expressiveness beyond unimodal flow priors. VMF enables efficient one-step inference while maintaining strong generation quality and diversity. Extensive experiments on four standard molecular benchmarks demonstrate that our model outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving higher novelty (e.g., 74.5% on PCDes) and diversity (up to 70.3%), and 100% validity across all datasets. Moreover, VMF requires only a number of function evaluations (NFE) equal to 1 for conditional generation and at most 5 for unconditional generation, offering 1-NFE conditional inference and improved wall-clock efficiency, especially relative to multi-step Transformer baselines. Our code is available at this link: https://github.com/Atik-Ahamed/MolSnap.

records.title: FLAb2: Benchmarking reveals that protein AI models cannot yet consistently predict developability properties.
records.abstract: We introduce the Fitness Landscape for Antibodies (FLAb2), the largest public benchmark for therapeutic antibody design, comprising developability data for over 4 million antibodies across 32 studies and covering 7 properties: thermostability, expression, aggregation, binding affinity, pharmacokinetics, polyreactivity, and immunogenicity. Evaluating 30 AI and biophysical models, we find that most (80%) fail to produce statistically significant correlations. No model performs well across all properties. Some pretrained models (IgLM, ProGen2, Chai-1, ESM2, ISM, and IgFold) show significant zero-shot correlations for select properties. Fine-tuning with ≥102 points helps for thermostability, aggregation, and binding though polyreactivity and pharmacokinetics lack sufficient data. With enough data (103 points), a fine-tuned one-hot encoding model matches billion-parameter models. Training data matters more than architecture, and intrinsic properties (thermostability) are predicted more readily than extrinsic ones (immunogenicity and pharmacokinetics). Partial correlation analysis shows that germline distance accounts for ∼37% of language models' apparent predictive power.

records.title: EvoSeq: A Eukaryotic Sequence-Function Profiling Platform for AI-Guided Engineering of Genome-Editing Enzymes.
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping protein engineering, yet progress remains constrained by the limited availability of scalable, normalized sequence-activity datasets and experimental benchmarks. Reported here is Evolution by Sequencing (EvoSeq), a sequencing-based profiling platform for genome-editing enzymes that links each variant to a reporter sequence change, enabling activity and variant sequence to be quantified together by next-generation sequencing. Representative sequencing-assisted workflows either require separate functional assays or were performed in bacteria. EvoSeq performs sequence-activity profiling in eukaryotic yeast system with reduced background by up to 95-fold compared to bacterial system, positioning EvoSeq as a pooled eukaryotic alternative to workflows that require separate functional assays and to approaches demonstrated primarily in bacteria. Application to adenine base editor evolution identifies variants with 1.4-fold higher on-target activity at a HBG gene target and threefold lower off-target editing at PCSK9 after mRNA-lipid nanoparticle validation in HepG2 cells. An intron-embedded homologous-recombination recording strategy further enables direct evolution of the large Cas12i nuclease CasY7 and supports active learning, increasing the hit rate of model-nominated mutational windows compared with manual selection. EvoSeq therefore provides an experimental benchmarking method for AI-guided protein-design algorithms and AI-compatible sequence-activity profiling platform for engineering genome editors in eukaryotic cells.

records.title: [Advances in ProteinMPNN-driven protein engineering].
records.abstract: Biomanufacturing is a key pathway for promoting the green transformation of conventional production methods. Its core bottleneck lies in the difficulty of natural enzymes to meet the requirements of industrial applications, necessitating the customized modification of enzyme molecules through protein engineering. Conventional semi-rational design is limited by a narrow sequence search space, heavy reliance on known structural information, and high experimental screening costs, which make it difficult to achieve precise design of industrial-grade enzyme molecules. In recent years, artificial intelligence-based protein design technologies represented by ProteinMPNN have made breakthrough progress and are driving a profound paradigm shift in protein engineering. This article systematically describes the technical principles, workflow, and methodological advantages of ProteinMPNN, compares it with Rosetta and other protein design models, and reviews the research progress of this technology in industrial enzyme engineering and biomanufacturing. On this basis, this article discusses current research hotspots and challenges in industrial application, and provides an outlook on future development directions and prospects for industrial implementation. It is expected to serve as a reference for fundamental research and industrial translation in synthetic biology and protein engineering.

records.title: Multi-omics integration maps the molecular architecture and clinical vulnerabilities of the MGUS-SMM-myeloma continuum.
records.abstract: Clinical frameworks for monoclonal gammopathies rely mainly on cytogenetics and serological biomarkers, but these approaches overlook epigenetic plasticity, microenvironmental remodeling, and metabolic adaptation that drive progression and therapeutic resistance. This review synthesizes recent multi-omic evidence to define a clinically oriented framework for risk stratification and early intervention. We performed a focused narrative review guided by SANRA principles. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from January 2015 to December 2025 using terms for multiple myeloma, monoclonal gammopathy, MGUS, smoldering myeloma, multi-omics, single-cell, spatial transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, epigenomics, and liquid biopsy. Original cohort and translational studies relevant to plasma cell disorders were prioritized. Genomics reveals structural variation, noncoding drivers, APOBEC mutagenesis, and subclonal evolution beyond FISH. Epigenomics links t(4;14)/NSD2 and chromatin accessibility to drug sensitivity and persister states. Single-cell transcriptomics exposes intraclonal heterogeneity and early immune dysfunction, while proteomics and metabolomics identify mRNA-protein discordance, metabolic dependencies, and sensitive residual disease detection. Integrative models can resolve clone-niche interactions that shape progression from MGUS/SMM to myeloma, although most require external validation. Multi-omics refines biological understanding and reveals actionable vulnerabilities in monoclonal gammopathies. Clinically useful implementation will require parsimonious, validated models combining existing assays with selected high-resolution modalities to improve precursor risk prediction and stratified early intervention.

records.title: Circulating tumor DNA for disease monitoring in bone sarcomas: clinical applications, challenges, and future perspectives.
records.abstract: Bone sarcomas (BSs) are rare, biologically heterogeneous malignancies for which disease recurrence and metastatic progression remain major determinants of poor patient outcomes. Therefore, reliable tools to aid the assessment of response to treatment, the detection of molecular residual disease (MRD) and the timely identification of disease recurrence are essential but still limited to conventional imaging and tissue-based approaches. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), a tumor-derived fraction of cell-free DNA detectable through liquid biopsy (LB), has emerged as a promising non-invasive biomarker capable of capturing dynamic molecular changes throughout the course of the disease. Increasing evidence supports its potential for postoperative surveillance, early relapse detection, response assessment and longitudinal monitoring. Nevertheless, several biological and technical barriers, including low ctDNA abundance, genomic heterogeneity among BS subtypes, and the lack of standardized analytical workflows continue to hinder widespread clinical implementation. This mini review provides an overview of the current landscape of ctDNA applications for MRD detection and disease monitoring in BSs, examines the key challenges to its clinical adoption, explores technological advances and outlines ongoing clinical studies that are expected to shape its future role in patient management.

records.title: The application of circulating tumor cells in endometrial cancer: A narrative review.
records.abstract: Endometrial cancer (EC) is increasingly common worldwide, and recurrence remains difficult to anticipate using clinicopathologic factors, static tumor molecular classification, imaging, or conventional serum markers alone. This narrative review evaluates circulating tumor cells (CTCs) as a cell-based liquid biopsy for EC, with emphasis on their biological rationale, detection technologies, and potential roles in risk assessment, surveillance, and minimal residual disease monitoring. CTCs preserve intact cellular morphology and phenotypic information that are not captured by circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), including protein expression, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-related features, cell clustering, and intercellular heterogeneity. Current EC studies remain small and methodologically diverse, but collectively suggest that CTC detection is feasible in selected early-stage, high-risk, advanced, and recurrent settings. Detection performance varies substantially according to platform design: CellSearch® provides standardized EpCAM-dependent enumeration but may underestimate EpCAM-low or EMT-shifted CTCs, whereas size-based, microfluidic, multimarker, and molecular approaches may improve sensitivity at the cost of requiring further specificity validation. With the continued development of CTC profiling, single-cell biopsy, and single-cell sequencing technologies, CTC analysis may move beyond enumeration toward phenotype- and subtype-informed characterization. This review highlights the need to clarify how The Cancer Genome Atlas molecular subtypes relate to CTC count, epithelial/mesenchymal phenotype, cluster status, and protein-marker expression. It also emphasizes that benign gynecologic conditions with invasive or inflammatory features, including endometriosis, should be incorporated into control cohorts to better define false-positive CTC or CTC-like events. Although CTC testing in EC remains in the clinical research stage, emerging automation, artificial intelligence-assisted image interpretation, and scalable microfluidic workflows may improve throughput, reproducibility, and cost-effectiveness. Clinical implementation will require analytical standardization, multicenter prospective validation, adequate benign and healthy controls, predefined clinical endpoints, direct comparison with ctDNA and serum biomarkers, and formal cost-effectiveness assessment.

records.title: Plasma ctDNA tumor fraction as an independent prognostic factor in metastatic colorectal cancer: Differential prognostic impact across treatment lines and irrespective of hepatic metastatic burden.
records.abstract: Quantitative circulating tumor DNA(ctDNA) Tumor Fraction (TF), algorithmically derived by comprehensive liquid biopsy profiling, captures systemic tumor burden, but its independent prognostic value in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), particularly relative to hepatic metastatic burden, remains incompletely characterized. We retrospectively analyzed baseline ctDNA TF in 284 consecutive mCRC patients profiled with FoundationOne Liquid CDx at University of Campania Luigi Vanvitelli (systematic testing, blood draw ≤4 weeks pre-treatment). TF was classified as High (>1%) or Low/Not Detected (≤1%). Primary endpoints were progression-free (PFS) and overall survival (OS); multivariable Cox proportional hazard models and line-stratified analyses were performed. Of 229 evaluable patients (80.6%), 153 (66.8%) were classified as High TF and 76 (33.2%) as Low/Not Detected. High ctDNA TF was independently associated with inferior PFS (HR 1.73, 95%CI 1.18-2.54; p = 0.005) and OS (HR 2.00, 95%CI 1.26-3.17; p = 0.003) in multivariable analysis. Hepatic metastases were not independently prognostic after adjustment for ctDNA TF (PFS p = 0.589; OS p = 0.585). The prognostic effect was concentrated in later lines of therapy (II-V+: PFS HR 2.40, p = 0.012; OS HR 2.92, p = 0.004), with no significant association in first-line patients. However, the formal interaction test between ctDNA TF and line of therapy did not reach statistical significance. Findings were consistent using also a 10% TF threshold (PFS HR 1.65, p = 0.006; OS HR 1.86, p = 0.004). High baseline ctDNA TF is an independent prognostic factor for shorter survival in mCRC, with the strongest prognostic effect observed in later treatment lines and independently of hepatic metastatic burden. These findings support prospective validation of ctDNA TF as a stratification factor in clinical trials.

records.title: Separating Signal from Noise: Applications, Tradeoffs, and Barriers in Nanotechnology-Based Liquid Biopsy for Cancer.
records.abstract: Noninvasive liquid biopsies have shown great promise in the field of cancer diagnostics. In this work we review liquid biopsy assays that have achieved regulatory approval, uncovering limitations that impact wide clinical adoption. We find assay sensitivity to be a central limitation particularly hindering screening assays aiming to detect early disease with low circulating target levels. Nanotechnology, including materials and devices engineered on the nano- and micrometer scale, enables signal amplification strategies to increase sensitivity and improve the detection of low-abundance biomarkers. While nanotechnology displays strong potential, there are interconnected barriers to clinical adoption including variability in manufacturing and complex workflows unfamiliar to physicians and unsuitable for clinical laboratories. Clinical translation is further constrained by an evolving regulatory landscape and variable Medicare/insurance coverage which are key determinants for physician acceptance. Addressing these barriers, alongside continued sensitivity and multiplexing capability improvements, will determine whether nanotechnology platforms can move from research settings into routine clinical practice and advance liquid biopsy diagnostics. While liquid biopsy techniques are unlikely to replace tissue testing, they may provide a valuable diagnostic complement.

records.title: Blood-Based Liquid Biopsy of Circulating Tumour DNA to Achieve Genomic Diagnosis for Glioma.
records.abstract: Liquid biopsy of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) facilitates genomic diagnosis and influences treatment decisions in many solid organ malignancies. However, its use in glioma, the most common primary brain tumour, has been limited to date. This is likely due to low concentration of tumour analytes within the plasma, assay heterogeneity, and lack of standardisation across studies thus far. While cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) contains greater concentrations of ctDNA than the peripheral circulation, repeated lumbar puncture is not clinically practical for longitudinal monitoring, and may be contraindicated in some patients. Comparatively, blood draw is minimally invasive, can be performed in almost all clinical settings, and is widely accepted as a screening modality by patients already. This narrative review discusses the current state of blood-based liquid biopsy in glioma, in addition to how this may influence clinical decision making and alter patient trajectories.
